text:
Alex: Quick sync—I'm worried about ambiguous semantics between the edge proxy and runtime sidecar for hosting-mode. We need a clear handshake so "private" never silently degrades to hosted.

Maya: Totally. What's the current failure mode?

Alex: When dedicated pool is saturated the runtime emits a soft-fallback and the sidecar sometimes rewrites headers. Ops dashboards show increased hosted traffic but we can't tell if it's allowed or accidental.

Rohit: That matches my traces. Sidecar code path A strips X-RW-Hosting when it proxies to the router, so the router assumes no constraint and routes to hosted.

Samuel: We should define a tiny, authoritative contract: LB/edge must be the ultimate arbiter of fallback. Sidecars can mark preferred_mode but can't override. If edge sees preferred_mode==private it must reply 409 rather than reroute.

Maya: Nice. So minimal fields: X-RW-Hosting-Mode (hosted|dedicated|private), X-RW-Fallback-Ok (true|false), X-RW-Rollout (id). Sidecars only write preferred_mode, LB normalizes and enforces.

Rohit: Implementation detail: add an Envoy filter that inspects tenant config cached in the LB and rejects requests that would cross boundary. Edge can also inject X-RW-Rollout when missing.

Samuel: We also need observable signals: counter infra.fallback_attempts{mode="private",reason="eviction"} and span tag hosting.mode for every root span. If we see a hosting.mode change mid-flight, that should generate an audit event.

Alex: Agreed. How do we handle older sidecars that don't emit preferred headers?

Maya: Two-phase compatibility: 1) Audit-only for 2 weeks: LB will log missing header and emit compatibility metric. 2) After audit window, LB enforces tenant policy (reject for private). We should notify customers in advance.

Rohit: Tests: runtime unit to ensure header pass-through; integration test where we simulate pool exhaustion and assert LB does not route to hosted for private tenants. CI job should flip the compatibility flag.

Samuel: Also add a small JSON error body for consistency: {"code":"HOSTING_VIOLATION","msg":"private tenant - fallback blocked"} so SDKs can special-case. Redact any tenant identifiers in logs.

Maya: Who owns rollout_id format? We should standardize to date+sequence like 20260321-001 in the RFC so dashboards can group.

Alex: I'll draft RFC for the header names, LB filter behavior, and metric names. Include a compatibility timeline and a playbook for migrating old sidecars.

DeployBot: CI result: canary runtime build passed 12/12 smoke tests. See https://ci.internal/c/1755550001 for logs.

Rohit: Action items: Alex RFC, Maya notify PMs and legal for customer notif, Samuel add metric/trace tags, I will prototype envoy filter. Target: land filters + tests in 2 sprints.

Maya: Quick note: make sure the LB rejects use 409 not 403. 403 implies auth, 409 implies policy conflict. SDKs prefer 409 for retries.

Alex: Good call. Thanks everyone. I'll post RFC link when done.

Samuel: +1, will start trace changes tomorrow.

Rohit: prototyping now, will ping when I have a WIP.

Maya: :thumbsup:
